newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Perry details Iraq response to US forces this month.
newsitem.headline: Perry details Iraq response to US forces this month.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Sunday that Iraq had rebuilt air defence units and fired six missiles at U.S. warplanes since U.S. missile strikes against Iraq in early September.
"For the security of this region, to continue Operation Southern Watch -- that is the linchpin of security and stability in this region," Perry told reporters in Bahrain.
"That Operation Southern Watch...just yesterday we had conducted more than 100 sorties over southern Iraq. That operation has been challenged by the Iraqis," Perry said.

"They challenged it by reconstituting air defence units in the area, they challenged it by moving mobile surface-to-air missiles into the area and they challenged it by firing six missiles at our planes. These were wild firings but nevertheless they were firings."
A U.S. military official confirmed to Reuters that Perry was referring to six missiles Iraq had fired since U.S. cruise missile attacks against Iraq on September 3 and 4.
Perry is on a visit to the Gulf to try to rally the Gulf War alliance against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein following Iraqi missile attacks against U.S. planes patrolling the no-fly zone.

Iraq said on Friday it would suspend its air defence attacks on U.S. and allied planes policing no-fly zones over southern and northern Iraq. There have been no reports of any Iraqi attacks since then.
"We will not tolerate threats to our air troops," Perry said.
Perry said he had "excellent" talks with Bahrain's Emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa and other ministers.
"We will do what is necessary, protect our mutual security in this region and Bahrain and the United States stand shoulder to shoulder," Perry said.
He said Washington will send 23 F-16s to Bahrain "as part of the military force we have in this area, generally that is providing security and stability for the whole region."
Bahrain said on Sunday it had agreed to host United States military planes on the island.
The official Gulf News Agency (GNA) quoted an official as saying Bahrain had "agreed to host a number of U.S. military planes on its territory".
GNA said Bahrain's acceptance of U.S. warplanes on the island was in the framework of a defence cooperation pact with the United States.

Washington has moved up additional warplanes to the Gulf including radar-evading Stealth fighter-bombers to Kuwait and B-52 bombers at the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia for possible military action against Iraq.
Bahrain is the administrative headquarters of the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet which operates an aircraft carrier battle group and other warships in the oil-rich region.
Perry later left Bahrain for Jeddah n and U.S. officials said he would hold talks with King Fahd of Saudi Arabia.

Earlier in Kuwait, Perry had held out the possibility of more strikes on Iraq and asked Kuwait to accept additional American troops on its soil to deter potential trouble from the Gulf state's former occupier.

He told a news conference that the United States "will take whatever action is necessary" to enforce an expanded southern Iraqi no-fly zone up to the 33rd parallel and to protect U.S. pilots patrolling it.

Perry said he had asked Kuwait's emir, Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, for permission to proceed with a plan announced by Washington on Friday to deploy several thousand more U.S. troops in the Gulf state.
The emir had replied that Kuwait would give its reply after Kuwait's Supreme Defence Council discussed it, Perry added.
